posts.body_html:
I love that more people are now working with them. I think one of the reasons they are rare is that they are very slow to divide. I've had mine since I was in high school and have only divided it twice during that time. I've always meant to get a colony started for seed production but it seemed impossible to find another genetically distinct plant until now.

Some things I have noticed from growing my one clone is that they seem to appreciate a little shade during the hottest parts of summer. They also grow perfectly fine in partial shade all year long too.

posts.body_html:
finally got these plants to bloom! How do you describe the frangrance? It's pungent, sweet, and I can see what people are saying about spicy but that smell doesn't register as spicy to me. It almost reminds me the aroma of walking into a cut flower shop, it really does smell great! My neighbor came over the other weekend and he's like "whoah, dude Mike, what's this thing?!!!" It really caught his attention, although he's a plant head too so go figure.

Interestingly enough, there is a slight variation in color from one clone to the next, some are lighter than the other! I have cross pollinated the flower heads to hopefully maintain genetic diversity. pics taken 4/14/25:













Only a small fraction of the plants flowered this spring, but there's a very good chance that they will all bloom next spring! They just weren't big enough this time around and given that they were just hardened off a few months ago, it's still pretty surprising that some of them flowered this season!



Notice the new growth is green in the middle, signifying that the temperatures are warming up and the plants are starting to bust out. They're really happy right now getting morning sun and bright indirect light for the rest of the day:

posts.body_html:
If your plants turn reddish during the winter dormancy period, don't worry, that is a normal response to cool temperatures and good light intensity. These plants thrive in morning sun and filtered light for the rest of the day.

Now that spring has arrived, these plants are back in full growth mode and are looking well! Photos taken 5/1/25:

posts.body_html:
So the plants were way underpotted last season to the point that the soil looked like mostly roots by the end of the grow season! It took HOURS to separate the plants from the massive tangle of roots!


So here's the interesting truth about this species: they are BULLETPROOF! I must have cut off half of the root system and they didn't wilt or flinch for a second!


This probably weighed 40lbs:


Looking amazing right after transplanting! Most of these appear to have have form an inflorescence bud, but it won't emerge until the spring:


So beautiful en masse, even when they're not blooming!


some big artichoke heads fully dormant, waiting for warmer weather:


Main flower bud in the middle, and no idea what those little things are on the side....side shoots? We will find out soon! I'm still new to growing these plants and have not seen them all the way through over the years:
